videoTitle: Why Your Honeymoon Might Feel Wrong (Even After 12 Years Together)
videoDescription: Feeling disconnected or regretful right after your wedding doesn't mean you married the wrong person. Research shows nearly half of newly married women experience post-wedding depression—and unresolved family conflict makes it worse. Get the full breakdown at mindtivate.com
script: You've been together twelve years, you just got married, and suddenly you're questioning everything. That's not rare—research shows nearly half of newly married women feel let down or depressed after the wedding, even when the relationship was solid before.

Marriage makes implicit things explicit. His family's disrespect and his failure to protect your boundaries suddenly feel permanent. The cake wasn't just cake—it was the one thing you asked for, and when his sister destroyed it, he didn't have your back.

In-law conflict is linked to declining marital satisfaction over time. If he doesn't see the tension as a problem, that's what you need to address—not whether you overreacted. This feeling is data. Trust it enough to talk about it.
Head to mindtivate.com for what actually helps when you're in this space.
